cases.quote: The Japanese "single line alignment method" is a process for setting alignment for a run of text that is shorter than a given line length. This method is frequently used for headings and poems. The following methods are available (see Figure 157).
cases.rationale: The rule names centering among the methods available for a run shorter than a given line length; the quantity it fixes is where the run's own characters sit — centered, with as equal a room on each side as the residual allows — and not the line's own reported extent, which follows from ADR-0017's definition of realized geometry applied to whichever method placed the residual rather than from anything §3.5.3 itself states. Two ideographs (亜亜, cl-19, no inter-character spacing of their own — Table 1's cl-19-against-cl-19 cell is blank) placed unaligned reach a natural extent of 2000 (two 1000-unit items, no gap between them); against a 3000-unit target that leaves a 1000-unit residual, and `jlreq_line::Alignment::Centered` splits it into two equal 500-unit shares (`jlreq_unit::distribute` over two equal weights, exact since 1000 divides evenly by two) and pushes the whole run in by the leading share alone, so the first ideograph sits at 500 and the second at 1500. The trailing 500 units are left unconsumed past the run's own end, reserved rather than walked, which is why the composed extent is 2500 and not the full 3000: `crate::Line::extent` reports what the cursor actually reached, and Centered's own trailing share is never one of the places it goes.

forbidden.why: This is `Alignment::LineEnd`'s own answer — the whole residual pushed in front of the run, reaching the target — and not `Centered`'s, which splits the residual rather than pushing all of it to one side; this case's own `alignment` names `centered`.
This is `Alignment::LineHead`'s own answer — the natural, unshifted placements, with the whole residual left unconsumed — and not `Centered`'s, which pushes half of it in from the start.
